title: Fruits Into Baskets III
summary: Given two arrays, fruits and baskets, each of length n, place each fruit type in the leftmost available basket with sufficient capacity, ensuring each basket holds only one type of fruit.
statement: Given two arrays, fruits and baskets, each of length n, place each fruit type in the leftmost available basket with sufficient capacity, ensuring each basket holds only one type of fruit. If a fruit type cannot be placed, it remains unplaced. Return the count of unplaced fruit types.
constraints: fruits and baskets have equal nonzero length and positive values.
Process fruits in order, placing each in the leftmost unused basket whose capacity is at least its amount.
Count fruits for which no qualifying basket remains.
hints: A segment maximum tells whether any basket in an interval can hold the current fruit.
Build a max segment tree and descend left first whenever that half has sufficient capacity.
If the root maximum is too small, count failure; otherwise find the leftmost qualifying leaf, set it to zero, and update ancestors.
Left-first descent gives the required earliest basket, while clearing leaves enforces one-time use.
editorial: Left-first descent gives the required earliest basket, while clearing leaves enforces one-time use.

tests.explanation: Four uses capacity five, two uses the first basket, and no basket can then hold five, so one fruit is unplaced.
Two uses the second basket; the first basket then holds one, so both are placed.
